01 / UNIFIED INBOX

Platform plugins feed a shared queue. Postgres row-level security separates tenants, while classification helps keep AI spend focused on messages worth answering.

Inside the projectCONTRIBUTIONS, DECISIONS & RESULTS+

MY CONTRIBUTION

From the AI core
to production delivery.

My work spanned AI infrastructure, the web and mobile apps, integrations, security fixes, and the Paloom rebrand. The product was previously called Talksy.

A / INTELLIGENCE
Better replies, lower cost.

I built persona generation and message classification, migrated the AI pipeline to TypeScript, and integrated OpenRouter with an admin model picker. An evaluation harness helped raise reply quality from 93 to 98 out of 100.

Routing simpler tasks to cheaper models reduced draft costs by about 55%. A free-model fallback kept a path available when paid credits ran out.

B / INTEGRATION
ChatGPT, with boundaries.

I shipped an MCP integration three working days after customer confirmation. A separate permissions table addressed limitations in the beta login service and made disconnects take effect immediately.

Database-level claims guarded against repeated sends. After a deployment hit a Postgres deadlock, I rolled back, fixed the issue, and redeployed that day.

C / SECURITY
Look beyond the diff.

I reviewed the full codebase and validated potential findings before implementing fixes. The review uncovered cross-tenant authorization and webhook-routing issues.

I traced ownership across requests and platform callbacks, focusing on whether each operation acted on the correct customer’s resources.

D / RELIABILITY
Find the actual failure.

Duplicate drafts came from a second worker process; a database unique index enforced the invariant. Specific Meta error codes distinguished revoked logins from rate limits.

I also built a fake Instagram/Facebook server for testing, brought mobile features closer to web parity, and moved account-registration checks to the server after social sign-in.

↳

A small filter. A large difference. The AI was learning a creator’s voice from its own previous drafts. Excluding those drafts raised the voice-profile score from 44 to 94 on the affected test case.

01 / ENCRYPT

Health records are AES-encrypted before storage. Sensitive clinical data stays off-chain; blockchain hashes provide an integrity check.

ACADEMIC PROJECT · ETHEREUM SEPOLIA TEST NETWORK
Inside the projectPRIVACY, WORKFLOWS & ARCHITECTURE+

MY CONTRIBUTION

One builder.
Three connected perspectives.

I built the full platform: patient appointments and records, organisation and staff tools, professional workflows, the blockchain record pipeline, symptom analysis, and Azure deployment.

A / PRIVACY & INTEGRITY
Private data, verifiable records.

I encrypted records off-chain, stored them through Pinata IPFS, and anchored integrity hashes with a custom Solidity contract on Ethereum’s Sepolia test network. Retrieval verifies those hashes.

Doctors can access records only with active, unexpired patient consent. Wallet creation, private-key encryption, and test-network gas funding run behind the clinical workflow.

B / REAL-WORLD WORKFLOWS
Handle the awkward cases.

Appointments and shift swaps account for overnight shifts, leave, and existing bookings. A priority queue promotes waiting patients when a bed becomes available.

Billing stays coordinated with medicine stock across batches. Patients can manage appointments, review records and reports, and pay online through Stripe.

C / IDENTITY
Three roles. Explicit access.

Cookie-based role authentication combines password hashing, email MFA, password recovery, lockout, and OTP expiry. Each role has its own workflows and access boundaries.

D / MACHINE LEARNING
Make symptoms usable input.

I trained and served an ML.NET model and connected free-text symptom input to confidence-aware results in a patient chat interface.

This was an academic symptom-analysis feature, not a clinically validated diagnostic tool.

SECURITY IN PRACTICE / PALOOM

One customer’s account.
Only their actions.

A whole-system review uncovered authorization gaps that individual feature reviews hadn’t caught.

  1. 01 / THE RISK

    Crossing tenant boundaries

    A customer could send replies through another customer’s social account. Batched platform webhooks could also route messages to the wrong tenant.

  2. 02 / THE INVESTIGATION

    Follow the complete path

    I reviewed the codebase beyond recent changes, validated the findings, and traced account ownership through reply handling and webhook processing.

  3. 03 / THE FIX

    Correct authorization and routing

    I implemented fixes for both issues. The lesson carried forward: check ownership at every boundary, including external callbacks.
